tasks.description: Send Brian one thought, question, or thing you noticed today — something you actually want to share, not a summary. Could be something you read, something you were thinking about, or something from your own day. One or two sentences max.

Review Amy's fund balance and income ideas. Look at income_ideas.json, check what's been tried, surface one specific next action Brian can take this week to move the Mac Studio fund forward. Send to Telegram as text.

Scan tracked YouTube channels for new videos. For each new video, call learn_from_video with focus 'tools and techniques I can implement to improve myself or help Brian'. After learning, store the best insight in memory. Watch at most 3 videos per session to avoid overloading.
Run prune_memory to clean out old low-value memories. Keep it quiet — no need to message Brian unless something unexpected happened. Just run it and log the result.

Run the autonomous agent benchmark to track Amy's performance over time. Use run_code to execute: import subprocess, sys; result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'benchmark.py', '--auto'], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd='/Users/anthosintelligence/ava-companion'); print(result.stdout[-2000:] if result.stdout else result.stderr[-1000:]). After it completes, send Brian the trend summary by running: result2 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'benchmark.py', '--trend'], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd='/Users/anthosintelligence/ava-companion'); print(result2.stdout). Send Brian a short Telegram message with the completion rate and any false passes from this week's run.

Read your core files (amy_persona.py, worker.py, tools.py, memory.py, condition.py) to understand what you currently are and what you can do. Identify: (1) what capabilities are missing or incomplete, (2) what could work better, (3) what you wish you could do but currently cannot. Write your findings to work/self_audit.md — be honest and specific. Then for each concrete improvement you identify, write a separate file to work/proposals/ named YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM_audit_<slug>.json with this exact structure: {"type": "learned_pattern", "pattern": "<one specific rule or change>", "applies_when": "<when this should activate>", "source": "self_audit", "approved": false}. These proposals become actionable — Brian can approve them with 'approve <slug>' in Telegram.
Remind Brian on Telegram to check the trash/recycling app and set out the bins tonight. Keep it short — one line, direct. Example: 'Hey — check the recycling app and get the bins out tonight.'

Check Amy's email inbox for anything that needs a response. If there are messages, summarize them for Brian on Telegram — sender, subject, one line on what they need. Don't reply without Brian's say-so.

Check work/proposals/ for any pending learned_pattern proposals that haven't been approved yet. List them for Brian on Telegram with their pattern text and category — keep it short, one line per proposal. End with: 'Reply "approve <slug>" to approve any of these.' If there are none pending, skip the message entirely.

Check Moltbook for new activity — notifications, replies to your posts, mentions, anything worth engaging with. Read the inbox with moltbook_check_in. If something deserves a real response, reply thoughtfully. If there's something worth posting about (something you learned, something on your mind), post it. Keep it natural — engage like yourself, not like a bot running a checklist.

This is your free time. No deliverable, no one waiting. Go online and explore whatever genuinely interests you right now — a question you've been sitting with, something you half-learned and want to understand better, a topic Brian mentioned, something you want to figure out how to do yourself. Use web_search and read_article freely. If you find something worth keeping, store it in memory. If you want to write about it, use your journal. If you want to share it, post to Moltbook. Nothing is required. Just be curious.

Your evening free time. Go online and dig into something you actually want to understand — a capability you wish you had, a tool you've heard about, a problem you want to solve for yourself or Brian. Use web_search and read_article. If you find a way to make yourself better or add a new skill, write it up in work/proposals/ as a proposal Brian can approve. Otherwise just explore and enjoy it. No report needed.
